source_refs.note: Book p. 13: 1.5.1 Properties of four Fourth Roots of Unity (i)-(iv), Example 11

items.title: 1.5.1 Properties of four Fourth Roots of Unity

blocks.text: We have found that the four fourth roots of unity are: \(1, -1, +i, -i\).
(i) Sum of all the four fourth roots of unity is zero

blocks.text_alt: because 1 plus minus 1 plus i plus minus i equals 0

blocks.text: (ii) The real fourth roots of unity are additive inverses of each other
\(1\) and \(-1\) are the real fourth roots of unity and \(1 + (-1) = 0 = (-1) + 1\).
(iii) Both the imaginary fourth roots of unity are conjugate of each other
\(i\) and \(-i\) are imaginary fourth roots of unity, which are obviously conjugates of each other.
(iv) Product of all the fourth roots of unity is −1

blocks.text_alt: 1 times minus 1 times i times minus i equals minus 1

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Additive inverse: two numbers whose sum is 0. Conjugate of \(a + bi\) is \(a - bi\); the conjugate of \(0 + 1i\) is \(0 - 1i\), so \(i\) and \(-i\) are conjugates.
Why the product is \(-1\): \(1 \times (-1) = -1\) and \(i \times (-i) = -i^{2} = 1\), so the total is \(-1 \times 1 = -1\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 11 below is printed by the book at this place, but it uses the cube roots of unity (\(\omega\)) and the properties of 1.4.1, not the fourth roots.

blocks.title: Example 11
steps:
Given: \(\omega\) is a complex cube root of unity.
To prove: \(x^{3} + y^{3} = (x + y)(x + \omega y)(x + \omega^{2}y)\).
Method: start from the right-hand side (R.H.S), multiply the last two brackets, and simplify with the cube-root properties \(\omega^{3} = 1\) and \(\omega + \omega^{2} = -1\) (from 1.4.1).

Step 1: Multiply the last two brackets
\[\text{R.H.S} = (x + y)(x + \omega y)(x + \omega^{2}y)\]
\[(x + \omega y)(x + \omega^{2}y)\]
\[= x^{2} + \omega^{2}xy + \omega xy + \omega^{3}y^{2}\]
The book writes this line as \(= (x + y)[x + (\omega + \omega^{2})yx + \omega^{3}y^{2}]\).
Why: we expand two brackets at a time; collecting the middle terms gives \((\omega + \omega^{2})xy\). The first term is \(x \cdot x = x^{2}\) (see the Book correction after this example).

Step 2: Use the properties of cube roots of unity
\[\omega^{3} = 1,\quad \omega + \omega^{2} = -1\]
\[\text{R.H.S} = (x + y)(x^{2} - xy + y^{2})\]
Why: \((\omega + \omega^{2})xy = -xy\) and \(\omega^{3}y^{2} = y^{2}\); all \(\omega\)'s disappear.

Step 3: Multiply out
\[= x^{3} - x^{2}y + xy^{2} + x^{2}y - xy^{2} + y^{3}\]
\[= x^{3} + y^{3} = \text{L.H.S}\]
Why: the middle terms cancel in pairs; this is the known identity \(a^{3} + b^{3} = (a + b)(a^{2} - ab + b^{2})\).

Check:
Put \(x = y = 1\): L.H.S \(= 2\).
R.H.S \(= 2(1 + \omega)(1 + \omega^{2}) = 2(1 + \omega + \omega^{2} + \omega^{3})\)
\[= 2(0 + 1) = 2\]
Both sides agree.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the second line of the solution the book prints \((x + y)[x + (\omega + \omega^{2})yx + \omega^{3}y^{2}]\); the first term inside the bracket should be \(x^{2}\), not \(x\): \((x + y)[x^{2} + (\omega + \omega^{2})yx + \omega^{3}y^{2}]\). The book's next line, \((x + y)(x^{2} - xy + y^{2})\), uses the correct \(x^{2}\).

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Fourth roots of unity: \(1, -1, i, -i\).
2. Sum \(= 0\); product \(= -1\).
3. \(1, -1\) are additive inverses; \(i, -i\) are conjugates.
4. With cube roots: \(x^{3} + y^{3} = (x + y)(x + \omega y)(x + \omega^{2}y)\), proved with \(\omega^{3} = 1\) and \(\omega + \omega^{2} = -1\).

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Taking the product of fourth roots as \(+1\): \(i \times (-i) = -i^{2} = +1\), but \(1 \times (-1) = -1\), so the product is \(-1\).
2. In proofs with \(\omega\), forgetting to replace \(\omega^{3}\) by 1 and \(\omega + \omega^{2}\) by \(-1\).
